newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom 1996 sales, earnings up.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom 1996 sales, earnings up.

text.p: German telecommunications group Deutsche Telekom AG, under pressure from investors to make a statement about the 1996 business year, said on Monday that sales rose six percent and earnings were above expectations.

The company said in an unexpected regulatory statement that sale grew to more than 63 billion marks, that it would pay as promised a dividend of 60 pfennigs per share on 1996 results and that it was able to cut financial debt by 10 billion marks.
"Deutsche Telekom will exceed previous estimates for the full year," chairman Ron Sommer said in the statement. "All in all the expectations of the board have been more than fulfilled."
Deutsche Telekom shares, listed on international stock exchanges in a partial privatisation last November, have lagged behind the general market trend in the past few weeks.

Analysts complained last week that the company has given no indication of its performance towards the end of the 1996 or whether its targets for 1996 would be met. Telekom said it would make a statement on 1996 earnings in March.
Telekom said the high level of its cash flow allowed it to finance investment and cut debt to around 82 billion marks at the end of 1996, a decline of 10 billion marks from 1995.

Excluding the workforce that of the Hungarian telephone company Matav, in which Deutsche Telekom has a stake, the company said its group workforce fell to 201,000 employees at the end of 1996, putting it half-way to its target of 170,000 by the year 2000.
